name: Scope the trace
intro: Answer these before any pixel is measured. Every answer decides which steps of the pipeline run and what the build script emits — nothing here is a preference.

sections.title: The job
sections.lead: What is being handed back, and whether you want to watch it happen.

options.label: A PDF
options.hint: a drawing set, a brochure or one sheet: every plan is found, cropped and labelled first, and you confirm the crops

questions.note: the file in library/Images/ or Designs/, or the path you will hand over

questions.ask: Does the sheet hold more than one plan?
questions.note: brochure sheets often carry two unit types, a key plan and a title block

options.label: Several — I'll say which
options.hint: title block, key plans and legends are masked out first

questions.note: the intake works this out from the sheet titles; say so only if you already know

options.label: Let the intake decide
options.hint: single, multi-level or master plan, from the titles; you see its answer with the crops

options.label: Several floors of ONE building
options.hint: traced as levels of one plan

options.label: A master plan
options.hint: site, roads and several buildings: one grouped JSON, each building a group

questions.ask: Before tracing, do you want to check the crops?

options.label: Yes, show me every crop and its label first
options.hint: the contact sheets plus a table; nothing is uploaded or traced until you agree

options.label: No, trust the labels
options.hint: wrong labels surface only at the overlay proof

options.label: Canvas plan JSON
options.hint: overlays the image exactly; this is always produced

options.label: Also a DXF
options.hint: hands off to the Canvas Json to Dxf skill afterwards

options.label: Also a headless 3D bake
options.hint: proves every attachment resolves

options.label: Also the overlay proof images
options.hint: the pictures, not just the numbers

questions.ask: How do you want it run?

options.label: Run it through and hand me the file
options.hint: fastest; accuracy over steering

options.label: Trace it on the live canvas while I watch
options.hint: staged, with a checkpoint before each stage; I can nudge a wall or flip a hinge as it goes

sections.title: Scale and orientation
sections.lead: Everything downstream inherits the scale. A wrong scale is not a visible mistake — it is a plan that looks right and measures wrong.

questions.ask: Where does the scale come from?

options.label: Printed room dimensions
options.hint: every one of them, fitted by least squares — the accurate route

options.label: An overall dimension or scale bar
options.hint: one number for the whole sheet

options.label: A dimension I will give you
Guess it from a known standard
options.hint: 0.9 m door leaf, 0.6 m counter — this is a guess and gets reported as one

options.label: I will set the scale myself in the app
options.hint: you click two points on a printed dimension; takes about ninety seconds

questions.ask: The dimension, and what it spans
questions.note: e.g. "13'0" across the master bedroom, inner face to inner face"

questions.ask: Should I check the two axes separately?
questions.note: worth it on a photographed or rescaled sheet, where horizontal and vertical scales differ

options.label: The compass on the drawing
options.hint: usually a small square outside the plan

options.label: A bearing I will give you
Assume the top of the sheet is north
options.hint: fine for a render; wrong for anything solar

options.label: I will click it myself in the app

questions.note: degrees clockwise from the top of the sheet

sections.title: What to trace
sections.lead: The levels are a ladder — each one includes everything above it. This is pixel measurement and your own reading of the drawing, not a box detector, so more detail costs time rather than accuracy.

questions.ask: How far should the trace go?

options.label: Centrelines only
options.hint: nodes and segments, nothing attached — a bare graph

options.label: Walls with real thickness
options.hint: adds the Wall object and per-wall thickness

options.label: Walls and openings
options.hint: adds doors, windows and leaf-less openings, cut into the wall runs

options.label: Everything
options.hint: adds rooms with their printed labels, and the furniture

options.label: RCC columns
options.hint: the darker blocks sitting on the wall lines

options.label: Room labels exactly as printed
options.hint: BEDROOM-2, LIVING / DINING

options.label: The north arrow as an object
Ducts and service shafts as spaces
options.hint: the boxes with a dashed X

options.label: One room
options.hint: its walls still need their neighbours measured to close; the design questions follow

questions.note: name them as the drawing prints them

questions.ask: What kind of room is it?
questions.note: this picks the design questions that follow the trace

options.label: Bedroom
options.hint: questions ready

options.label: Living room
options.hint: no questions written yet

options.label: Kitchen
options.hint: no questions written yet

options.label: Bathroom
options.hint: no questions written yet

options.label: Something else
options.hint: trace only, no design questions

questions.ask: After the trace, ask me how the room should look?
questions.note: the design questions — headboard, wardrobe shutters, lighting. Say no to trace the room and stop there.
the canvas is metric either way; this is what the report and the labels read

options.label: Measure each wall
options.hint: exterior and partitions differ; this is the accurate route

options.label: One nominal value everywhere
options.hint: faster, and wrong wherever the drawing disagrees

questions.ask: When a printed size and the drawn walls disagree
questions.note: they do disagree — a printed 8'×5' toilet often does not fit between the faces at any scale

options.label: Make the printed numbers exact
options.hint: solve wall lines from the printed spans; every room label then reads as printed

options.label: Follow the drawn walls
options.hint: keep the measured lines; labels may read a few inches off

questions.ask: Will the editor be open with ?agent=1 ?
questions.note: the last verification check imports the file through the app's own importer; without it that check cannot run

questions.ask: Anything about this plan I should know?
questions.note: a dimension you know is misprinted, an alcove excluded from a printed size, a symbol you want read a particular way

flags.says: You have asked to set the scale yourself, but also for the trace to run straight through and hand back a file. In batch mode there is nobody to hand the app to.
flags.resolution: Either switch to the live canvas mode, or let the scale come from the printed dimensions.

flags.says: Clicking north yourself needs the app open, and this run does not stop for you.
flags.resolution: Use the compass on the drawing, give a bearing, or switch to live mode.

flags.says: A centrelines-only trace has nothing for a column to sit on — columns are objects on wall lines.
flags.resolution: Take the detail up to walls, or drop the columns.

flags.says: Room labels are carried by space rings, and this detail level does not emit spaces.
flags.resolution: Take the detail to Everything, or drop the labels.

flags.says: A scale guessed from a standard door leaf is a guess. Every dimension in the result inherits it.
flags.resolution: If the sheet prints any real dimension anywhere — even one — use it instead.

flags.says: Solving wall lines from printed spans adds half a thickness at each end, so one nominal thickness will push rooms off wherever the real wall differs.
flags.resolution: Measure the thicknesses, or accept that the labels will not read exactly as printed.

flags.says: Without the editor open, the trace can be proved by numbers and by the overlay image, but not through the importer the user actually uses.
flags.resolution: Open the editor with ?agent=1 before the run ends, or accept three checks instead of four.

flags.says: Only the bedroom has design questions written. This room type would reach the Room Renderer form with nothing to ask.
flags.resolution: Trace it and stop there, or write that room type's questions file first.

flags.says: The design questions are prefilled from the traced openings — window width, which door is the entry — and a centrelines-only trace has none of them.
flags.resolution: Take the detail to walls and openings, or expect to type those by hand.

flags.says: A room's walls are shared with its neighbours, so the bands either side still have to be measured for the ring to close.
flags.resolution: Nothing to change — the saving is in what gets authored, not in what gets measured.

flags.says: Several sheets, or a whole site, is not a live job: the live route draws one plan on one canvas.
flags.resolution: Run it through (batch), or pick the one sheet you want to watch and trace that crop live.

flags.says: A master plan places whole buildings on a site; tracing one room of it has no site to place it on.
flags.resolution: Trace the whole master plan, or answer 'one floor plan' and name the sheet in Which pages.

flags.says: Nobody checks what the intake decided. A key plan or a per-floor site sheet labelled wrongly is traced as a building.
flags.resolution: Check the crops. It is one look at the contact sheets.
